stem: A disaster-risk review distinguishes I: reducing structural vulnerability, II: developing ability to act on warnings, and III: restoring disrupted services after impact. Project A reinforces a bridge without changing the storm forecast; B teaches households how to interpret a warning and rehearse a route; C restores a damaged water line. Which mapping and limitation are justified under RA 10121?

choices.text: A addresses I, B addresses II and C addresses III; changing vulnerability need not change the storm hazard.
A addresses I, B addresses III and C addresses II; changing vulnerability need not change the storm hazard.
A addresses II, B addresses I and C addresses III; restoring the water line establishes pre-impact preparedness.
A addresses I, B addresses II and C addresses III; unchanged storm intensity means A has not reduced disaster risk.

explanation: Reinforcement mitigates structural impacts, warning interpretation and rehearsal build preparedness, and post-impact restoration is rehabilitation. Hazard intensity and vulnerability are distinct: unchanged storm intensity does not show unchanged risk. Two alternatives have the same correct mapping, requiring evaluation of the limitation as well.

stem: A town compares two disaster-risk proposals. In K, residents attend a presentation but cannot influence assessment or remedy selection; radio numbers are its only readiness measure. In L, residents identify risks, choose remedies and monitor implementation; its evaluation also tests whether messages are understood and evacuation actions can be performed. Which paired assessment best applies community-based DRRM and early-warning definitions?

choices.text: K establishes community-based decision-making through attendance, while L assesses response ability beyond equipment counts.
K does not establish community-based decision-making, while radio numbers alone establish whether recipients can act.
K does not establish active community decision-making or response ability; L addresses both through participation and functional checks.
K and L equally establish community-based decision-making, while only L examines response ability.

explanation: Community-based DRRM requires active roles in risk analysis, treatment and monitoring, not attendance alone. Warning effectiveness also concerns understanding and ability to act, which radio inventories do not measure. L addresses both; alternatives preserve only one distinction or confuse attendance with decision-making.

stem: A climate review considers K: elevated storage powered by higher-emission generators; L: lower-emission power with unchanged flood exposure; M: lower-emission power plus flood-safe storage. The reviewer distinguishes an action's adaptation purpose from its emissions effect and from meeting both objectives. Which assessment keeps all three distinctions?

choices.text: K includes adaptation, L includes mitigation and M includes both; K's adaptation therefore makes K an emissions-reduction measure too.
K includes mitigation, L includes adaptation and M includes both; L's lower emissions do not themselves relocate exposed stores.
K includes adaptation, L includes mitigation and M includes both; M's dual role means mitigation and adaptation are interchangeable classifications.
K includes adaptation, L includes mitigation and M includes both; K's higher emissions do not negate its adaptation role but prevent inferring emissions reduction.

explanation: Adjustment to impacts and intervention on emissions are separate axes. K adjusts exposure but does not reduce emissions, L reduces emissions without the stated exposure remedy, and M combines them. Each distractor retains a correct fragment while reversing classifications or improperly merging separate objectives.

P is partial; Q fully establishes gender mainstreaming, while R addresses both definitions.

choices.text: Leo's writing validates his waiver, but Neri's lack of writing invalidates hers; coercion remains prohibited
Neither waiver meets both requirements, and counsel's presence or a signature does not authorize coercion
Both waivers are valid because each satisfies one safeguard; coercion remains prohibited
Neither waiver meets both requirements, but a valid waiver would authorize physical coercion

explanation: Section 12(1) requires writing and counsel together; each waiver lacks one. Section 12(2) independently forbids coercion. Knowing only the waiver rule leaves two plausible alternatives; the separate coercion safeguard resolves them.

stem: Accused J was arraigned, duly notified and unjustifiably absent. Accused K was notified but has not yet been arraigned. A court says both absences prove guilt and allow the same trial-in-absence exception. Which review is best under Article III, Section 14(2)?

choices.text: The stated exception covers J and K; neither absence proves guilt
The exception covers J only; J's absence by itself proves guilt
The stated exception covers J only; neither absence by itself displaces presumed innocence
The exception covers neither J nor K; both absences defeat presumed innocence

explanation: The exception requires arraignment plus notice and unjustifiable absence; only J meets the stated conditions. Presumed innocence remains separate and cannot be replaced by treating absence as proof. The alternatives deliberately mix the two rules.

stem: A covered employee files a statement showing assets and debts but omits a business interest. She also proposes using classified office data to help a bidder without accepting payment. Which analysis correctly separates Sections 7(c) and 8?

choices.text: The statement is incomplete; lack of payment makes the proposed data use permissible
The statement is complete if net worth is correct; the proposed data use is prohibited
The statement is complete if net worth is correct; lack of payment makes the data use permissible
The statement is incomplete; conferring undue advantage with nonpublic official data can be prohibited without payment

explanation: Section 8 includes business interests beyond assets, liabilities and net worth. Section 7(c) covers undue advantage to anyone without requiring personal payment. Correct arithmetic cannot cure omitted disclosure, and absence of compensation does not cure misuse.

stem: A professional leaves an agency and, six months later, plans private work on an unrelated matter outside that agency. A separate proposed assignment is a professional matter before the former agency. Assume no other restriction or conflict applies. Which assessment matches Section 7(b)'s post-separation exception?

choices.text: The general private-practice prohibition is excepted, but the former-agency matter remains subject to the one-year bar
Both engagements are prohibited because all private professional work is barred for one year
The unrelated engagement is prohibited, but the former-agency matter is exempt
Both engagements are exempt because retirement ends every Section 7(b) restriction

explanation: The post-separation paragraph excepts general private professional practice from the one-year continuation, while retaining that bar for professional matters before the former office. Neither a blanket ban nor a blanket exemption preserves both parts.
